title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous pages: X is a space stratified by a poset I. The closed strata X_i are closed in X, and the family is locally finite. The open strata are X_i^* = X_i \ ∪_{j<i} X_j. The non-empty X_i^* partition X, and X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j^*. I carries the topology in which the closure of {i} is {j ≤ i}, i.e. the closed sets are the down-sets: this is the Alexandrov topology, with closed = order ideal.

For J ⊂ I, (93) sets X_J^* = ∪_{j∈J} X_j^* and X_J = ∪_{j∈J} X_j. Equivalently, if s: X → I sends x to the index of the open stratum containing it, then X_J^* = s^{-1}(J).

This page draws the elementary consequences.
- (94) J ↦ X_J^* commutes with arbitrary unions and intersections, since the X_i^* form a partition. In particular X_∅^* = ∅ and X_I^* = X.
- (95) X_J^* ⊂ X_J = X_{J̄}^*. Hence if J is closed (a down-set), X_J = X_J^*, and this set is closed: it is a locally finite union of closed sets.
- (96) X_J^* = X_{J̄}^* \ X_{J̄\J}^*. If J is locally closed in I (a convex subset; the word on the page is hard to read), then J_0 = J̄\J is closed, so X_J^* is locally closed.
- (97) Under the density axiom (Strat 5: X_i^* dense in X_i), the closure of X_J^* is X_J = X_{J̄}^* = X_J^* ⊔ X_{J̄\J}^*. Hence X_J^* is closed iff X_{J̄\J}^* = ∅.
- If the stratification is moreover faithful (all X_i^* non-empty), this happens iff J̄ = J, i.e. iff J is closed.
- (98) If L ⊂ I is open, then J = I\L is closed, so X_L^* = ∁_X X_J^* is open.
- A struck-out attempt defines the 'boundary' Ẋ_J = closure(X_J^*) \ X_J^*.

In modern terms, the page verifies that s: X → I is continuous for the Alexandrov topology, that preimages of locally closed subsets are locally closed, and that under density plus faithfulness s 'reflects' closedness. It is foundational bookkeeping for the theory of stratified spaces and conical neighbourhoods developed in the rest of the manuscript.
errors: (95) and (97) silently use the local finiteness of the family (X_i), which is needed for a union of closed strata, or a union of closures, to be closed. Local finiteness is assumed on the neighbouring page, so this is consistent.
The equivalence 'X_J^* closed iff X^*_{J̄\J} = ∅' needs Strat 5. Without density only one direction holds. The text places it after the Strat 5 hypothesis, so this is fine, though compressed.
The struck-out first line 'X^*_J = X_{J̄}' is false in general; Grothendieck rightly deleted it.

ideas.what: A stratification indexed by a poset I, viewed via the map X→I, with I given the topology whose closed sets are down-sets. X_J^* is the preimage of J, and its compatibility with unions and intersections is just the behaviour of preimages.
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified space: a continuous map X → P with the Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A, c. 2009–2017); also Treumann, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Barwick–Glasman–Haine
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame stratified spaces but not this formalism explicitly; unsure about other texts

ideas.what: Preimages of closed, open and locally closed (convex) subsets of I are closed, open and locally closed strata unions. Under density, the closure of X_J^* is X_{J̄}^*.
ideas.modern_name: Continuity of the stratification map; the frontier condition in union form

ideas.what: For a faithful dense stratification, X_J^* is closed iff J is closed in I, so I embeds in P(X) as a family of closed sets.
ideas.modern_name: Faithful (surjective) stratification; recovering the poset from the strata

missed.claim: Around 1981–82 Grothendieck already formulates stratifications as poset-indexed families with I topologized by down-closures (Alexandrov topology), working systematically with X_J^* = s^{-1}(J). This is essentially the modern 'X → P continuous' definition used in exodromy and higher-categorical stratified homotopy theory, which is usually attributed to much later authors.
missed.quote: Si J est une partie de I, on pose X_J^* = ∪_{j∈J} X_j^* ... (98) X^*_L = ∁_X X^*_J est ouvert (si L⊂I est ouvert)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority note for the poset-stratified formalism. Mathematically the content is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains elementary, correct set-theoretic and topological lemmas about poset-indexed stratifications. The only point of interest is the early, clean appearance of the 'continuous map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology' viewpoint, which is now standard.
transcription_corrections: The page number at top left reads '43' (notebook numbering), not '93'.
The word before 'J_0 est fermé' appears to be 'bande' or a similar word; mathematically it must mean 'J localement fermé' (convex), since that is exactly what makes J̄\J closed.
The rotated left-margin note seems to read roughly: 'de dimension... X_J^* est le plus petit fermé de X de la forme X^*_?, puis ... ouvert dans X^*_J'. It is partially illegible.
